turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mr. Deshmukh, come, sit. I will check your pressure and pulse before the doctor calls you.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes sister. This toe is killing me, I could hardly get my chappal on. My wife said stay home only, but I thought let me just come.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Blood pressure is one thirty eight over eighty eight, pulse is ninety two, oxygen is ninety eight percent, and temperature is thirty six point nine celsius.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Ninety two, that is high no? I was rushing from the auto, and with this pain also.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Pain and hurrying can do that. Keep the foot up on the stool, doctor is coming.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Good morning Anil. I am Dr. Mehta. Tell me, what has brought you in today?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, my right big toe. It is swollen and paining like anything since last night. I could not sleep properly, even the bedsheet on it was too much.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): That sounds very sore. Did it come on suddenly, or was it building through the day?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Suddenly only. I was fine at dinner, watching the match, and around eleven it started throbbing. By morning it was red and hot also.
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): My neighbour had some foot thing last month, fungus he said, he was putting cream. I told him mine is not like that at all.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): So red, hot, swollen, very painful, right big toe, from last night. Any fever, or are you feeling unwell otherwise?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. I am a bit tired from not sleeping, that is all. Appetite is fine, I had idli in the morning.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Have you had anything like this before?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, same kind of thing, about a year back. Left toe that time I think, or maybe the same right one, I am getting confused. It settled in four five days.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do you remember what treatment you were given?

[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Some painkiller, I think, from the local doctor, and he did a blood test. They said the uric acid was borderline. I don't have the paper, my wife keeps the file and I forgot it at home.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Borderline, but no actual number?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No number, doctor. Just borderline. He said not to worry if it does not come back. And here I am, na.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any other problems, blood pressure, sugar, anything like that?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): BP is there, for five-ish years now. I take a water tablet every morning for it. Sugar is not there, they checked last year.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do you know the name of that water tablet, and the dose?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Hydrochlorothiazide, twenty five milligram, one tablet in the morning. My physician in Pune started it. I don't miss it, I keep the strip near the toothbrush.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any other regular medicines? Allopurinol, painkillers, anything?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing else regular. Sometimes I take a Crocin if I have headache, but not nowadays.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to a medicine or a food?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that. I can eat everything.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): What about alcohol? Tell me how that looks in a normal week.

[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Weekend only. Saturday Sunday I have beer with friends, two or three bottles. Weekdays I don't touch it. Last Saturday was my cousin's birthday, biryani and all, so maybe four bottles, we sat late.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): A bit more than usual, then. Any injury to that foot, a twist or a knock?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no injury. I did not fall or anything. I was careful only.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Alright. Let me look. Can you take the sock off for me?

[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Wait, actually. Yesterday evening I kicked the wooden chair in the hall, with this same right foot. I said some words and then I forgot about it. It did not feel that hard.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): So there was a knock, even if it seemed small. Does the pain get worse when you move the toe?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): If I bend it, it is terrible. Keeping it up is a little better. Walking I cannot do.
[SEG0035] person_1 (NURSE): Foot is supported. The skin over that toe is quite red and shiny, doctor.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thank you, sister. Anil, I will press very gently around the joint.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Ah, that is the spot, the base of the big toe. Please, not too much.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): The right first metatarsophalangeal joint is hot, swollen and exquisitely tender. Skin is intact, no wound, the other toes look alright, and the foot pulses are fine.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): So not a fracture? My uncle had a fracture, big plaster, off work for weeks, and his factory supervisor was after him the whole time.

[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): I am not thinking of a fracture from what I see. This pattern, the sudden severe pain and swelling of the big toe, after beer and with a water tablet, is very much how gout presents. The chair may have stirred it, but I would not call it a simple bruise.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Gout. My father had gout in his knee when he was older. Every winter he would complain.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): That is useful to know. I would like a blood uric acid today, and kidney function as well, since you are on the water tablet. We will send those now.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Last time they said borderline only. Will this one tell you for sure?
[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): In the middle of an attack the level can even look normal, so it guides us, it does not prove it alone. Still worth doing.

[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): For the pain I want to start colchicine, point five milligram. Two tablets now, then one tablet after one hour, and after that one tablet twice a day for three days. If you get loose motions, stop it and let us know.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay, colchicine. My stomach is a little sensitive sometimes. Is there a painkiller type of option also?

[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): An anti-inflammatory, naproxen, five hundred milligram twice a day with food for five days, can be used. With the sensitive stomach and the beer over the weekend, I would rather start colchicine. If the colchicine upsets you badly, we can switch to naproxen, provided the kidney test is acceptable.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): So colchicine first, and the naproxen only if this one does not suit.
[SEG0049] person_3 (DOCTOR): Exactly. Please do not take both together, and no extra ibuprofen from the chemist.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): Understood. And the beer? My friends will definitely ask.

[SEG0051] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hold the beer until this settles, and after that, fewer weekend bottles will help these attacks. Keep the foot up, ice in a cloth for about ten minutes at a time, and drink enough water.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Ice I can manage. Next Sunday there is a match but I will skip the beer, promise. Water also I will take.

[SEG0053] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come back in one week, we will see the toe and the blood results. If the pain is getting worse, or you develop fever, or the redness is spreading up the foot, come earlier, do not wait.
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): One week, yes. Should I continue the water tablet?

[SEG0055] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes, continue the hydrochlorothiazide as usual for now. We will not stop it in the middle of this. Later your physician can look at a different BP tablet if the attacks keep coming.
[SEG0056] person_1 (NURSE): I will take the blood before you go, uric acid and kidney function. You have had breakfast?
[SEG0057] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes sister, idli around eight. Arm is fine. Thank you doctor, I will start the colchicine today itself.
